bugs: No sku length check: a sku over 255 chars passes row validation and goes to upsert into string(255). On MySQL/Postgres that fails the whole request with a 500 (or truncates silently) instead of producing a row error (app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:94).

Rows are split on physical lines (fgets), so a quoted field containing a newline breaks into two rows. Probe: '"E\nX",4' gives a column-count error on one line and then imports the garbage sku 'X"'. impl-2 and impl-3 share this.
antipatterns: The docblock return shape array{sku:int, quantity:int} leaves out the 'count' key the method actually returns (app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:65)
The error message echoes the raw quantity back unbounded, so a very long cell produces a very long error string (app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:101)
Redundant empty-batch guard: Eloquent upsert already returns early on empty input (app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:112)
Uses a (float) comparison for the overflow check where an integer comparison would do (app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:100)
strengths: The best memory profile: it streams with fgets and flushes upserts every 500 rows, and fclose sits in a finally block
Thin invokable controller, Form Request and single-purpose action. The header failure throws a ValidationException, so the 422 comes out in Laravel's standard shape
Handles BOM, CRLF, header case and spacing correctly, ignores blank lines while still counting them, and dedupes repeated skus within a batch
Rich Pest tests: a dataset of per-error messages, extra columns, batch boundary, semicolon delimiter, empty file, non-file and oversize cases
Uses the modern #[Fillable] attribute, casts() method and a factory

bugs: Rows are split on physical lines (fgets), so a quoted field containing a newline breaks into two rows. Probe: '"E\nX",4' gives a column-count error on line 8 and then imports sku 'X"' from line 9.
antipatterns: Holds every valid row in memory and upserts only after the whole file is read, even though it streams the input. Bounded by the 5 MB cap, but it undercuts the streaming (app/Actions/ImportStockCsv.php:46-57)
The tests call Http::preventStrayRequests(), which has nothing to do with this feature (tests/Feature/StockImportTest.php:15)
Trims the sku twice when building each row (app/Actions/ImportStockCsv.php:46-47)
strengths: Streams the file with fgets, closes the handle in finally, and upserts in chunks
Validates sku length (≤255) and the unsigned-int quantity range, so a bad row cannot cause a 500
Thin invokable controller, Form Request, invokable action and a named route. The header failure comes back as a standard 422 via ValidationException
A match(true) expression keeps row validation concise

The most thorough tests: precise line numbers with blank lines, whitespace-only sku, uint boundary, 1200-row chunking, a file at exactly 5 MB passing, an oversize file failing, a non-file value, a PDF and a PNG

bugs: Blank lines before the header are skipped, so the header can sit on line 3 and the file is still accepted. The spec says the header is line 1 (app/Services/StockCsvParser.php:27-41).
Rows are split on physical lines (preg_split), so a quoted field containing a newline breaks apart. Probe: '"E\nX",4' imports sku 'X"'.
antipatterns: Reads the whole upload into memory with ->get() and then preg_splits it into an array of lines instead of streaming (app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:15, app/Services/StockCsvParser.php:18)

The persistence logic (building records, chunked upsert) lives in the controller while parsing lives in a service, so responsibility is split awkwardly (app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:23-32)
Returns null as a sentinel for a bad header, which the controller then turns into a ValidationException; throwing directly would be clearer (app/Services/StockCsvParser.php:37,64)
Sets created_at/updated_at by hand and lists updated_at among the update columns, though Eloquent upsert already does both (app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:27,31)
The extra strlen(ltrim($q,'0')) > 10 check is redundant next to the (int) comparison (app/Services/StockCsvParser.php:56)
Numeric sku array keys turn into ints and need a (string) cast back (app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:27)
The model has no casts and no factory; the tests use StockLevel::create directly
strengths: Pairs extensions:csv with mimetypes, a strict and explicit upload check, and tests a PNG disguised as .csv
Checks sku length and the uint range
Correct BOM, CRLF and LF handling, header case and spacing, and blank-line counting
Solid core Pest tests with a dataset for missing headers

v.rationale:
All three pass their own suites (22, 17 and 25 tests). All three handle BOM, CRLF, header order, case and spacing, blank lines, line numbers, the uint bound, and 422 for a bad header or a non-CSV file. All three also split rows on physical lines, so a quoted multiline field breaks apart.

impl-2 ranks first. It streams the input with safe handle cleanup, validates sku length so a bad row can't cause a DB error, keeps a clean invokable controller → action → Form Request structure, and has the most thorough tests, including the exact 5 MB boundary. Its main weakness is that it buffers all valid rows before upserting.

impl-1 is nearly identical in structure and streams upserts better. It loses on a real gap: there is no sku length check, so on MySQL/Postgres a >255-character sku turns the whole import into a 500 instead of a row error. It also has a wrong docblock shape.

impl-3 ranks last. It loads the whole file into memory, splits persistence between controller and service, uses a null sentinel, sets timestamps that Eloquent upsert already handles, and accepts a header that isn't on line 1. It also has the thinnest tests.
